GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY
Date: 01/27/2026

Second recurrence of adult granulosa cell tumor, right ovary. Six cycles carboplatin/paclitaxel completed 01/08/2026. Also grade 1 endometrioid endometrial carcinoma on megestrol 80 mg twice daily since 03/2025.

Tolerated chemotherapy with fatigue and nausea, no admissions.
Exam: firm lower abdominal mass, nontender, similar to September.
Ultrasound: solid right ovarian mass about 10 cm, essentially unchanged.

Impression: stable disease without meaningful response this time.
Plan: gynecology to repeat endometrial sampling as planned; return in about six weeks to discuss surgery.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGY
Date of visit: 03/02/2026

Follow-up of known recurrent ovarian granulosa cell tumor and grade 1 endometrial carcinoma on megestrol. Irregular uterine bleeding for about six months, abdomen continuing to enlarge, a full feeling in the pelvis and occasional pelvic pain. Finished chemotherapy in January.

PSH: laparoscopic left salpingo-oophorectomy with staging 09/2023. Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, megestrol 80 mg twice daily, omeprazole, acetaminophen, diclofenac gel. NKDA. No family history of cancer.

Exam: BP 135/85. Palpable nontender mass in the lower abdomen. Pelvic: firm, irregularly shaped mass arising from the pelvis. Breasts: mild tenderness on both sides, no discrete mass, no nipple discharge.

Labs: hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, platelets 250 K/uL; estradiol elevated; testosterone normal; CA-125 normal.
Transvaginal ultrasound: 10 cm solid ovarian mass with internal blood flow.

Procedure: endometrial biopsy for the bleeding. Pathology (final 03/06): thickened endometrium, no evidence of malignancy - the carcinoma has not persisted on progestin.

Plan: results sent to gynecologic oncology, appointment 03/12 to plan surgery.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

Date: 03/12/2026

Recurrent adult granulosa cell tumor, 10 cm right ovarian mass, stable after second-line carboplatin/paclitaxel; ongoing estrogen production with bleeding and breast tenderness. Endometrial biopsy 03/02: no malignancy on megestrol.

She is now ready for surgery. Plan: exploratory laparotomy, total abdominal hysterectomy, right salpingo-oophorectomy and resection of the pelvic mass, scheduled 04/07/2026. Consent signed. Requesting pre-operative medical evaluation from her primary care physician.

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op evaluation requested by gyn onc for laparotomy, TAH, RSO and resection of pelvic mass on 4/7.

Functional capacity: climbs two flights at the library without stopping, walks 30 minutes, >4 METs. No chest pain, dyspnea, orthopnea, palpitations or syncope. No personal or family bleeding or clotting history. Prior anesthesia (2023 laparoscopy) uneventful. Never smoker.

Meds: HCTZ 25, amlodipine 5, omeprazole 20, megestrol 80 BID, acetaminophen PRN, diclofenac gel PRN. NKDA.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, BP at goal. Airway unremarkable. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen with firm lower abdominal mass, nontender. Calves soft, no edema.

A/P: 60F, low-risk patient for elevated-risk surgery. HTN controlled. RCRI 0. No further cardiac testing needed.
- Hold HCTZ the morning of surgery; take amlodipine and omeprazole with a sip of water.
- Megestrol per surgical team (carries VTE risk; they will advise when to stop and plan prophylaxis).
- BMP, CBC today; letter to surgeon.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 04/07/2026, discharged 04/10/2026
Service: Gynecologic Oncology

Diagnoses: recurrent adult granulosa cell tumor, right ovary; grade 1 endometrioid endometrial carcinoma treated with megestrol.

Procedure 04/07/2026: exploratory laparotomy (low midline), total abdominal hysterectomy, right salpingo-oophorectomy, resection of the pelvic mass. Findings: 10 cm solid right ovarian mass, mobile, removed intact; uterus normal size; no ascites; no visible disease elsewhere in the abdomen or pelvis. No complications.

Course: mechanical and pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis in hospital; diet advanced POD 1; ambulating; pain controlled on oral acetaminophen by POD 2; voiding. Incision clean.

Discharge medications: megestrol STOPPED. Continue hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: gynecologic oncology in 2 weeks for incision check and pathology review; no lifting over 10 lb for 6 weeks; PCP visit within 2 weeks.

reports.text: A. Uterus and cervix, total hysterectomy: endometrium with progestin-related changes; no residual carcinoma. Myometrium and cervix unremarkable. B. Right ovary and fallopian tube with mass: adult granulosa cell tumor, recurrent, 10.4 cm, capsule intact; completely resected, margins negative. Fallopian tube without tumor.
reports.conclusion: Recurrent adult granulosa cell tumor, right ovary, 10.4 cm, completely resected. No residual endometrial carcinoma.

documents.title: Office Visit - After Hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks after laparotomy with TAH, RSO and resection of the right ovarian mass (4/7-4/10). Pathology: recurrent adult granulosa cell tumor 10.4 cm, completely removed, margins negative; no cancer left in the uterus. Megestrol stopped at discharge. Her gyn onc incision check is next week.

Pain mild, acetaminophen twice a day. Eating normally, bowels moving. No bleeding. No leg swelling or breathlessness. Walking the hallway and the street a bit farther each day.

Vitals per flowsheet, afebrile, BP at goal. Midline incision healing, no redness or drainage. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near the incision. Calves soft and nontender.

A/P
1. Recurrent granulosa cell tumor s/p resection; endometrial carcinoma s/p hysterectomy, no residual. Gyn onc surveillance. Updated problem list: s/p hysterectomy; postmenopausal bleeding resolved.
2. HTN - continue HCTZ and amlodipine.
3. CBC today after surgery.
4. Return to work per surgeon, likely late May.

1. HTN controlled - continue both. BMP today.
2. Granulosa cell tumor and endometrial carcinoma, treated - gyn onc surveillance, next visit in September.
3. GERD/hiatal hernia - continue omeprazole.
